keyEvents.impact: Born amid coups and pan-Arab rivalries; two decades of chronic instability followed

keyEvents.event: Loss of the Golan Heights to Israel in the Six-Day War
keyEvents.impact: Permanent territorial grievance and a frozen front with Israel that defined Ba'athist legitimacy

keyEvents.event: Hama massacre crushes the Muslim Brotherhood uprising
keyEvents.impact: Tens of thousands killed; fear and sectarian security rule became the regime's operating system

keyEvents.event: Uprising against Bashar al-Assad escalates into civil war
keyEvents.impact: Over half a million dead, half the population displaced, and the country carved up by foreign powers and militias

keyEvents.event: Russian military intervention rescues the Assad regime
keyEvents.impact: Locked Syria into dependence on Moscow and Tehran and froze the war for nearly a decade

keyEvents.event: Readmission to the Arab League and the February earthquake
keyEvents.impact: Arab normalization with Assad seemed to cement his survival even as the economy collapsed

keyEvents.event: HTS-led offensive topples Assad on 8 December; Israel seizes the Golan buffer zone and destroys most of the Syrian military
keyEvents.impact: End of 54 years of Assad rule; Iran's land bridge to Hezbollah severed; a new Sunni Islamist-rooted government inherits a ruined state

keyEvents.event: Ahmed al-Sharaa named interim president; coastal Alawite and Suwayda Druze massacres; US and EU lift sanctions and Sharaa visits the White House
keyEvents.impact: International rehabilitation of the new order, shadowed by sectarian violence and fears of minority persecution

keyEvents.event: January offensive against the Kurdish-led SDF ends in integration deals; US-mediated security talks with Israel collapse over the buffer zone
keyEvents.impact: Damascus reasserts control over the northeast and its oil, but the Israeli occupation of the south remains unresolved

history.narrative: A shattered state rebuilding under a former jihadist commander turned pragmatic president, courting Turkey, the Gulf and Washington for money and legitimacy. Its central challenge is holding together a mosaic of Alawites, Druze, Kurds and Sunni Islamists while Israeli troops sit on its southern soil.

redLines.description: Partition of Syria or foreign-backed autonomy for the Kurdish northeast, Druze south or Alawite coast
Permanent Israeli annexation of the post-2024 buffer zone or advance toward Damascus
Return of Iranian-backed militias or a Hezbollah supply corridor through Syrian territory

internalDivisions.name: Alawite, Druze and Christian minorities fearful of Sunni Islamist rule
Kurdish northeast and the incomplete integration of the SDF
Hardline jihadist factions and ISIS remnants versus the pragmatic transitional government

goals.description: Consolidate central authority over all armed factions, the SDF and the Druze south
Secure Gulf and Western reconstruction money now that sanctions have been lifted
Negotiate an Israeli withdrawal to the 1974 disengagement lines without war
Defeat ISIS remnants and prevent a return of Iranian influence
